h: Monks, Markets and a Medieval Battle
p: AirHop is on the northern edge of Shrewsbury, handy for the A49 and the A5, which makes it a straightforward run in from Telford, Oswestry or mid Wales. Just north of town is the site of the Battle of Shrewsbury, fought in 1403 between Henry IV and Harry Hotspur, and the church of St Mary Magdalene at Battlefield was built to remember those who died there. It's a fascinating little detour for history buffs.

Back in the centre, Shrewsbury Abbey has a lovely link to fiction: it's the home of Brother Cadfael, the monk detective in Ellis Peters' novels. Even if the kids haven't heard of him, the grand old abbey church is worth a look.
For lunch, the Market Hall is a real local favourite, with independent food stalls and cafés serving everything from hot snacks to proper sit-down meals. It's a good place to refuel and people-watch.
Every August, The Quarry park hosts the Shrewsbury Flower Show, a long-running event with displays, entertainment and fireworks. If you visit around then, expect the town to be buzzing.

Outside town, Attingham Park at Atcham is a National Trust estate with a grand mansion, deer park and woodland walks, and Haughmond Hill offers woodland trails and views back over the town. For bigger walks, the Shropshire Hills are within easy reach, with the Long Mynd and Carding Mill Valley near Church Stretton a family favourite.
Shrewsbury is a compact, walkable town with plenty of hills, so pack comfy shoes for later. Your legs will thank you after all that bouncing.
And if the weather turns, the town's independent shops and cafés make a cosy rainy-day stroll.
